newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama to slash tariffs on building materials.
newsitem.headline: Panama to slash tariffs on building materials.

text.p: Panama will slash import tariffs on construction materials to 10 percent, the Ministry of Planning and Economic Policy said Thursday.
Effective Septempter 1, import duties on more than 100 construction industry products, including steel, cement, zinc, aluminum and several varieties of wood, will drop to 10 percent from 40 percent.
"The reduction in import duties is part of an ongoing process in making our economy more competitive," Juan Francisco Aleman, the ministry's chief of staff, told Reuters.
In addition, Panama will lower tariffs on cooking oils, flour and other ingredients used in making bread by 30 percentage points, Aleman said.

"What we want to achieve is to be more within the parameters set in other Latin American countries," he said. "If you compared Panama's tariff structure last year with the rest of the region, we had fallen behind. Now we are in line or even ahead of other countries in the region."
(( -- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom, 507-223 7739))
